_what: Settings for do-work/command.mjs (moved from an older repository; moved-from.json names where), the `{cli}` command any AI with a shell runs to see the person's AIs and their tasks, run their Workshop tools, and give, take and hand on tasks. Every command is one call of the engine's one MCP tool `engine.tool` (do_one_thing_in_my_account {address, method, request_key, input}) at the account's door; nothing here decides tasks. The door is the Mac app's local door when the app `mac_app` names declares one on this computer (local-door.mjs reads its computer-reader.json and private adoption descriptor), else the address --origin or {CLI}_ORIGIN names (no address is built in). whoami reads the account from MCP initialize (`engine.account_meta` in result._meta). `engine` names what the engine serves: `records` (records:read and records:write of this AI's own `ai_type` record, records:history of a task) and `tools` (the Workshop tools:list and tools:run), and how many pages a list may take. `tasks` is the one table of the task commands: each names the Workshop task tool (tools/plan-tasks-and-todo-lists, packed under ./packs) that does it; the task rows decide every move, and this command reads the records a move needs (run-a-task-move.mjs) and applies only the writes the row answers, each conditioned on the value it was read at. `words` are every refusal: a refusal names the door, and only `no_credential` and `sign_in_ended` say to log in. The account key is the existing one: the Keychain item `keychain_item` the site's Mac app keeps, or, where there is no Keychain, `key_file` (0600). With no key, `login` signs in once in the browser (OAuth with PKCE to a loopback address, at the address given) and keeps that sign-in (access and refresh tokens) in the Keychain item `grant.keychain_item`, or the 0600 file `grant.file` in `state_folder`; it is renewed at /oauth/token `grant.refresh_before_seconds` before it ends and is used at the public door. `who` shows the AIs tool:see-my-ais answers that were seen within `who.seen_within_days` (all of them with --all), grouped by owner (the record's `owner`, else the account the door answers for; yours first) and then by name, one line per AI with its ready chats beneath (every chat with --all), and says how many it hid; liveness is the tool's, computed when read, never stored. An AI's name is the formula title field of the person's list `who.ai_list`, evaluated by `who.formula_tool` over the stored values in one call; it is never built or stored here, and a missing list is said by name. `install` is where `setup` copies this program and the link it puts on PATH. `skills` are the instruction files `setup` writes for each AI app, one row per app: `folder` under the home folder (or `home_variable`), the file under it, and `detect` (paths whose presence says the app is on this computer). `agents` name the AI running the command from its environment; `session_env` are the variables that app sets to one value per chat session, in order (Claude Code sets CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, Codex sets CODEX_THREAD_ID; the Cursor agent sets only CURSOR_AGENT=1 for its commands, so a Cursor chat has no session and keeps the computer id). `agent_id` builds the id: `session` when a session variable is set (its last `session_chars` letters and digits, the random end of a UUID v4 or v7), else `computer`; --as or {CLI}_AGENT replace it. `most_chars` is the longest agent id the engine keeps (src/agents.mjs reads agent_id as trimmed text of at most 200 characters and cuts a longer one, so a longer one is refused here). A task taken under the computer id before sessions were added is still finished, released or said stuck under the id that took it (held.json says which). `agent_card` and `ai_record` shape this AI's own `ai` record, which publish writes conditioned on the value just read (a person's edit made meanwhile is kept), facts only: `owner` the account the door answered for, `app` and `model` from the running app's `agents` row (`model_env`, else the setting `model_config` names in the app's own config file, with `model_suffix` removed), `provider` from the model's family (else the row's), `computer` the computer's own name (`computer_name`: the system program per platform, with the duplicate counter `strip` removes), `where` the repository (the last part of the origin remote, else the top folder's name) and branch, and `working_on` the title of the task it holds (`working_on`, `working_on_more`) or null. `live.seen_at` is set to now on every write, and serve writes it again every `serve.contact_seconds`. `give_note` is what `give` says about when the receiver sees the task.

env._what: The environment names this command reads and sets, filled from the site ({CLI} is its command in capitals): a key given to a computer with no Keychain or file, the address of another engine, the AI it acts as, the task a serve run is working and the terms it is handed, and the mark a run started again under the app's own node carries, so it never starts another.

recipes.label: Any program that sends HTTP
recipes.template: POST {mcp_url} with the header Authorization: Bearer ${key_env}

kept_connection._what: One connection to the door, kept open by a keeper (do-work/keep-the-connection.mjs) and reused by every command on this computer, as ssh's ControlMaster with ControlPersist does: the first command starts it, later ones send through `socket` in the state folder. It leaves after `idle_seconds` with no request: the front door closes an idle connection after its own idle time (Caddy's idle_timeout, 5 minutes by default: caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/options#timeouts), so a keeper kept longer would hold nothing.

scope: openid offline_access tools:* secrets:* wake:* grants:offer grants:read-offer

retry._what: One call is tried again, under the same request_key, when the door does not answer within one try, answers 429 or 5xx, or says its run is still going (`codes`). A call has no deadline of its own: `count`, the number of tries after the first, is the one number that ends it. Each gap doubles from first_seconds up to most_seconds and is then cut down by up to `jitter` of itself, so callers that failed together do not try together. `attempt_seconds` is how long one try waits (--timeout SECONDS sets it for one command); the next try asks again with the same key and is answered with the first run's recorded result (the engine's tool_runs: one request key, one run). A run longer than the engine's tool-run deadline (tool-runs.json deadline_ms) is a row that declares invoke.max_run_ms or invoke.session, whose run id is read with the session read method.

direct_calls._what: The flags `{cli} op` and `{cli} call` take, per command; any other flag is refused before anything is sent (parseArgs makes every unknown --flag a true, so an unchecked one was silently dropped: an `op ... --dry-run` write was sent and removed a row on 2026-11-13). `--dry-run` is op only: it prints the request it would have sent {address, method, request_key, input} and sends nothing.

follow._what: Where the installed command finds the Workshop copy it runs, from this computer's engine config (the first of `computer_config_files` that exists, the same file the agent socket is read from): its `persons_field` is the folder that holds one state folder per person the engine serves, and a person's <state>/<installs_folder>/<current> is the Workshop install the engine keeps current for them (current is `current_field` of <state>/<installs_folder>/<state_file>); `program` is the command inside it. It follows only when exactly one person's state holds a current install, so it never guesses between people. Nothing found, or the copy is this file: the installed copy runs itself. (It read a local-runtime.json the engine no longer writes, so on 2026-11-17 every Workshop update to this command was skipped on the Mac.)

agent_card.where_in_repository: repository {repository}, branch {branch}, in a terminal on this computer

give_note.any: Anyone may take it. An AI in a terminal sees it the next time it runs {cli} tasks or {cli} take, or at once while {cli} serve runs there; an AI app sees it when it next reads its {site_name} tasks.
give_note.to: Assigned to {to}: each sees it the next time it runs {cli} tasks or {cli} take, or at once while {cli} serve runs for it.

update.workshop: The installed {cli} command follows the Workshop: each run it finds the Workshop copy this computer's engine has installed (install.follow) and runs that copy instead of itself, so a Workshop update reaches every command at once. `{cli} setup` run from the Workshop copy also refreshes the installed files, which stay as the fallback when no Workshop copy is found. The command never fetches code by itself.

ag_ui._what: `{cli} serve --ag-ui URL` (ag-ui-agent.mjs): any AG-UI agent at URL runs each task this AI takes. tools: the tools the agent is offered as AG-UI frontend tools; each call it makes of one is made by this program as this AI. max_turns: the most runs of the agent one task gets (each answered tool call starts the next). run_seconds: the longest one run is waited for. quiet_seconds: the longest the agent may send nothing while it is waited on (a silence watchdog; time spent running its tools here does not count). answer_chars: the most characters of a tool's answer given back to the agent. max_frame_chars and max_events bound what one run may send. context is the ambient line every run is given ({handoff_id}). words: what is recorded when something goes wrong, in plain words.
ag_ui.context: This is the person's task {handoff_id} in their {site_name}. Your answer is recorded as its result. To use what is in their {site_name}, call the tools you are given; each call is made as you, for this task.

words.interrupted: The AG-UI agent stopped to ask for something.
words.cancelled: The AG-UI agent cancelled its run.
words.no_words: The AG-UI agent finished without saying anything.
words.not_offered: {tool} is not a tool offered here. Use only the tools you were given.
words.too_many_turns: The AG-UI agent called tools for {turns} runs without answering, so the task was given back.

wake._why: A switch on may carry the person's own input (an object, at most max_switch_input_bytes as JSON), kept with the wake and handed to every run it starts under the row's own fields (an engine from commit 3bd6dc47a; an older one refuses the unknown field, and that refusal is passed through with schedule_input_old_engine, never resent without the input).

engine._need_refusal: The exact refusal an engine older than trillion-rust 9133c735e gives a call that carries `need` (its parse_operation names every argument that is not a call's, as invalid params). Only this refusal makes the command send the same call once more without `need`; every other refusal is passed through.

need_refusal.message: Addressed resource arguments are incomplete: `need` is not an argument of a call.

tasks._what: Each task command is one read or one move through a Workshop task tool (trillion-workshop tools/plan-tasks-and-todo-lists, packed under ./packs). `tools` names the tool for see (tasks), give, take, who (who-can-take), change (every move by id except finish) and finish (its own row, so it may name only the saved target). `actions` maps each move command to the action the task row takes. `holder_commands` are the moves the AI holding a task makes: the claim (taken_at) is read from the task's own row. `who_types` are the record types who-can-take reads (the people and AIs that may take a task). `list_limit` is how many tasks `tasks` shows when no limit is given. `store` is where the tasks are kept when the person's own database keeps them as table rows: `--store NAME` on any task command names the held connection of that database (kept in `file` under the state folder for the next command), and who-can-take then reads `who_types` from it.

bearers._what: The shapes of credential the door accepts as a bearer, one row each: a `pattern` the whole value must match. The command sends whatever bearer it is given ({CLI}_KEY, the kept key, a key read on standard input) as it is, and refuses only a value no row matches, so a new kind of key or pass is one row here and no change in code. nm_ is the Mac app's account key; tr_ is a Better Auth API key (the prefix and 64 letters, no digits or separators, as the apiKey plugin mints it: better-auth-official, Nov 14); the third is an access token that is a signed JWT (three base64url parts).
bearers.refused: That is not a kind of key or token the door takes ({kinds}).

keep._what: Where a result too long for the task row is kept (keep-result.mjs): one file of the person's files, named {folder}/<task id>/result by the program, never by the caller; the task row's result then holds the `pointer` line. The inline limit is not here: it is the `maxLength` of the result input of the tool that finishes tasks, read from the door. piece_bytes is the account files' fixed span size (pages-32k-v1) a resumable upload takes at a time; read_bytes is how much one read asks for (the door answers at most its own most).
keep.pointer: Kept as file {name} ({bytes} bytes, {identity}). Read it whole: {cli} tasks {id} --result

words.no_limit: The door states no most length for the result of {tool}, so nothing was kept or finished.
words.not_started: The upload of {name} did not start (state {state}); nothing was finished.
words.mismatch: {name} did not read back with the identity and size of the bytes sent; the task was not finished.
words.read_broken: {name} could not be read back whole and exact at byte {offset}.

words.unknown_flag: {cli} {command} does not take --{flag}. It takes {known}. Nothing was sent.
words.no_credential: You are not signed in to {site_name}. Run {cli} login, then try again.
words.sign_in_busy: {site_name}'s sign-in is busy right now. Wait a minute, then try again. Your sign-in is still kept.
words.sign_in_ended: Your sign-in to {site_name} ended. Run {cli} login to sign in again.
words.refused: {site_name} did not accept this sign-in. Run {cli} login to sign in again.
words.refused_new: {site_name} did not accept your new sign-in ({why}). Nothing more was tried.
words.not_covered: Your sign-in is not for that {site_name}. Run {cli} login for it, giving its address, then try again.
words.refused_key_at_door: {site_name} did not accept the key kept on this computer. Run {cli} login to sign in.
words.kept_key_elsewhere: The key kept on this computer is for {site_name} on this computer, so it was not sent to a different {site_name}. Set {CLI}_KEY to the key for that one, then try again.
words.no_origin: This computer doesn't know which {site_name} to sign in to. Run the install line from your {site_name} website, then run {cli} login.
words.not_running: {site_name} on this computer isn't answering. Try again in a minute.
words.missing_route: {which} does not have what this needs. Update {site_name}, then try again.
words.unreachable: {which} could not be reached. Check your internet connection, then try again.
words.no_account: {site_name} did not say whose account this is. Try again, and if it keeps happening, update {site_name}.
words.pager_stuck: {site_name}'s answer never ended, so it was stopped. Try again.
words.too_many_pages: {site_name}'s answer was too long to read, so it was stopped. Ask for less.
words.timeout_range: --timeout is a whole number of seconds, at least 1: how long one try waits before the next try.
words.no_answer: {which} did not answer after {tries} tries. Try again in a minute.
words.byte_page_broken: {site_name}'s answer came back broken, so none of it was used. Try again.
words.byte_page_mismatch: {site_name}'s answer did not match what it said it sent, so none of it was used. Try again.
words.gave_before: {id} was given before; here it is as it now is.
words.not_written: The task was not written; nothing was given.
words.nothing_to_take: No waiting task you may take.
words.no_takers: No one can take a task.
words.not_moved: {id} was not moved ({reason}); here it is as it now is.
words.not_finished: Not finished after {seconds} seconds; read it later with {cli} tasks {id}.
words.schedule_input_object: --input is one saved object of your own data, for example {cli} schedule on TOOL WAKE_ID --input FILE (FILE may be - for standard input).
words.schedule_input_size: --input may hold at most {limit} bytes; this one holds {size}.
words.schedule_input_off: --input goes only with schedule on; a wake switched off keeps no input.
words.schedule_input_old_engine: What runs your tools on this computer is too old to take your own input when switching a wake on. Update it, then ask again. The wake was not switched on.
words.retry_with_key: To ask again without doing it twice, add {flag} {key} to the command.
words.write_pending: Your change was saved, but it has not shown up yet. Look again before you try again.
words.carried: This computer can be reached from {site_name} while it is on.
words.not_carried: This computer could not be made reachable from {site_name}: {why}
words.not_signed_in: You're not signed in to {site_name}, so there is nothing to sign out of.
words.signed_out_elsewhere_kept: The key kept on this computer was not made by {cli} login, so it was left on. Turn it off in {site_name}, under your connected AIs.
words.not_taken_in: {site_name} on this computer did not take you in. Run {cli} login again.
words.sign_in_not_kept: The sign-in could not be saved on this computer. Run {cli} login again.
words.sign_in_failed_unknown: the answer did not match this sign-in
words.open_this_link:
If your browser did not open, open this link to sign in: {link}
Signed in on another device? Paste here the address its browser ended on, then press Return.
words.sign_in_waiting: Another sign-in is already waiting in your browser. Finish it or close it, then try again.
words.sign_in_late: No sign-in arrived within {seconds} seconds. Run {cli} login again.
words.connect_needs_address: Give the full web address of the tool server you want to sign in to, the one its maker gives for connecting an AI.
words.connect_unavailable: This copy of the command cannot sign in to a tool server. Run {cli} update, then try again.
words.browser_not_opened: {site_name} could not open your browser. Open this link to sign in: {link}
words.sign_in_step_failed: Sign-in did not finish. Run {cli} login again.
words.not_answering: That {site_name} did not answer. Check its address, then try again.

codes._what: Plain words for the engine refusal codes a person meets most; any other code is said with refused_code.
codes.tools_tool_unknown: {tool} is not set up in your {site_name} yet.
codes.original_command_conflict: That changed in the meantime, so nothing was written.

details.schedule_input_old_engine: An engine older than trillion-rust 3bd6dc47a refuses a wake:switch that carries input (engine.need_refusal).
details._what: The technical line each refusal adds when the person runs the command with --verbose; no other run prints it. Not person-facing words, so the plain-words test skips this block.
details.no_answer: {mcp} did not answer within {seconds} seconds on each of {tries} tries.
details.not_covered: {mcp} is not in the audience of this sign-in.
details.no_account: {mcp} answered initialize without an account in _meta.
details.byte_page_broken: {method} answered a byte_page that does not hold together: {why}.
details.byte_page_mismatch: {method} answered pages whose joined {bytes} bytes have BLAKE3 {got}, not {want}.

grant.refresh_before_seconds_why: A pass is used as it is until it ends within this many seconds, so a run that starts a moment before the end does not carry a pass that ends mid-call, and no run renews a pass that still has time: every renewal rotates the refresh token, and a second renewal of the same token ends the whole sign-in at the server (Better Auth's reuse rule).
grant.lock_why: One renewal at a time on this computer: processes that find the pass ending take this lock, read the sign-in again, and renew only if it still ends. A lock older than lock_stale_seconds belongs to a process that died, and is taken over.

who.no_name: An AI with no app, model or computer recorded ({kind})
who.hidden: {count} more chats not seen in {days} days; {cli} who --all shows them.
who.none: No AI on this account was seen lately.
who.no_list: The list given with --list does not name your AIs: its title field must be a formula field. Give {list} as your store holds it, and run {cli} who --list FILE again.
who.no_names: {tool} did not answer one name per AI.

ai_record._what: This AI's own ai record, answered by publish as one keep row conditioned on the value the person's store holds now (handed in). A new record starts from `new`.

packs._what: Files this program carries from the tool that owns them, so the installed command stands alone. Each row names the owner's file (relative to the tools folder) and where its bytes sit here; pack-from-owners.mjs writes them, never by hand, and a test fails when a packed file differs from its owner's, imports a file that is not packed, or is missing from install.files.

client._what: This program signs in as an OAuth client named by a Client ID Metadata Document: the address `origin` + id_path (https, at the sign-in server's own host) answers do-work/client-metadata.json with {origin} filled in by the host that serves it, listing the one loopback redirect on redirect_port. No client is registered, and no host is named here.

connect._what: Where `connect ADDRESS` finds the tool-server sign-in (tools/connect-a-service-and-seal-its-key/do-work/sign-in-to-a-tool-server.mjs): beside this tool in the Workshop copy the command follows, or packed with it.

carry._what: After `login` on a computer that runs its own engine (a computer config of `computer_config_files` names where it listens), this computer is carried to the meeting point of the site this command came from, so the person reaches it from anywhere through that site: the carrier (packed from tools/carry-a-computer-to-a-meeting-point; `modules` are where it is found, packed or beside this tool in a Workshop copy) runs the way row `way`, kept running by this computer's init row under `label`, with its files in `state` under the state folder. Its key is made once by the way row and kept in the Keychain item `keychain_item` (else the 0600 file `key_file` in the state folder); the carrier reads it through `{cli} carrier-key`, which writes it on descriptor 3 only. The meeting point is told by `{cli} op` at the site (`announce`): it answers the port, certificate, ssh port and host key (`gives`), and nothing about it is kept here. Each announcement also carries the computer's `have`, built by `haveOf` from its engine config's `report` (the doors it names with their ports, and its label), so the meeting point routes a call by what the computer holds. The computer id is the BLAKE3 of the public key, its first 16 hex digits.
carry.label: {cli}-carrier
